Explore the Pathland repo at /Users/michael/Development/michaelkrog/Pathland to understand how the DOM renderer (TypeScript bundle, built to dist/pathland-dom-renderer.js, content-hashed as dom-renderer-<sha256>.js with pointer file _pathland/dom-renderer.current) is currently served in the Spring Boot starter and Quarkus extension.

I need a very thorough understanding. Please find and report:

1. In `lib/java/pathland-spring-boot-starter/`: every file/class that serves or references static assets, the DOM renderer bundle, HTML, CSS, `_pathland/` paths, resource handlers, controllers, auto-configuration. Show the relevant code snippets with file paths and line numbers.

2. In `lib/java/pathland-quarkus/` and `lib/java/pathland-quarkus-deployment/`: same thing — everything that serves/references the DOM renderer bundle, assets, `_pathland/`, resource routing, SSR endpoints, WebSocket, static file handling. Show code snippets with paths and line numbers.

3. In `lib/java/pathland-server-core/`: how SSR renders HTML and what URLs/paths it emits for the DOM renderer script, CSS, assets. Any config/seam for asset serving. Show code.

4. How the demos (`lib/java/pathland-spring-boot-demo/`, `lib/java/pathland-quarkus-demo/`) themselves serve the DOM renderer bundle currently. Do they have their own static resource dirs / controllers / config? Show all relevant files and snippets (application.properties, controllers, src/main/resources structure).

5. How the DOM renderer bundle gets built and copied (look under lib/typescript/, scripts/, pom.xml files, package.json, any maven plugins / npm scripts). Show the build wiring and where the bundle ends up (dist path, copied locations).

6. Any existing tests related to serving assets / DOM renderer / HTML rendering in these modules.

Report findings organized by module with concrete file paths, line numbers and code excerpts. Do not modify anything.
I'll explore the repo systematically. Let me start with a broad structural survey and targeted searches in parallel.

1: // Copy the built bundle into both demo modules' static resource dirs so the
2: // Maven jars stay self-contained and both demos serve the SAME artifact. The
3: // bundle lives under the reserved framework prefix `/_pathland/` (spec).
4: //
5: // The served filename carries a sha-256 content hash (`dom-renderer-<hash>.js`)
6: // so a new bundle always changes the URL — the scripts are served with
7: // `immutable` cache headers, and a fresh name is the only thing that busts the
8: // cache. A tiny pointer manifest `dom-renderer.current` is written next to the
9: // copies so the SSR layer emits the right <script src> without re-hashing:
10: //
11: //   dom-renderer-<sha256-12>.js
12: //   sha384-<base64>
13: //
14: // The second line is the Subresource Integrity digest for the script tag. Stale
15: // `dom-renderer-*.js` (and the pre-hash fixed `dom-renderer.js`) are pruned so
16: // the dirs never accumulate.
17: import { createHash } from "node:crypto";
18: import { copyFileSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, readdirSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
19: import { dirname, join, resolve } from "node:path";
20: import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
21: 
22: const root = resolve(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "..");
23: const source = resolve(root, "dist/pathland-dom-renderer.js");
24: const bundle = readFileSync(source);
25: const hash = createHash("sha256").update(bundle).digest("hex").slice(0, 12);
26: const integrity = "sha384-" + createHash("sha384").update(bundle).digest("base64");
27: const name = `dom-renderer-${hash}.js`;
28: const manifest = "dom-renderer.current";
29: 
30: const targets = [
31:   resolve(root, "../java/pathland-quarkus-demo/src/main/resources/META-INF/resources/_pathland"),
32:   resolve(root, "../java/pathland-spring-boot-demo/src/main/resources/static/_pathland"),
33: ];
34: 
35: for (const dir of targets) {
36:   mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
37: 
38:   for (const entry of readdirSync(dir)) {
39:     if (entry === name || entry === manifest) continue;
40:     if (!entry.startsWith("dom-renderer-") && entry !== "dom-renderer.js") continue;
41:     rmSync(join(dir, entry));
42:     console.log(`pruned stale ${entry} <- ${dir.replace(root, "…")}/`);
43:   }
44: 
45:   const dest = resolve(dir, name);
46:   copyFileSync(source, dest);
47:   console.log(`copied -> ${dest.replace(root, "…")}`);
48: 
49:   writeFileSync(resolve(dir, manifest), name + "\n" + integrity + "\n");
50:   console.log(`wrote   -> ${resolve(dir, manifest).replace(root, "…")}`);
51: 
52:   // The per-window-id service worker (issue #155) is copied verbatim under a STABLE
53:   // name: the browser re-fetches it to byte-compare for updates, so it must NOT be
54:   // content-hashed (unlike the bundle) and is served `no-cache`.
55:   copyFileSync(resolve(root, "sw.js"), resolve(dir, "sw.js"));
56:   console.log(`copied -> ${resolve(dir, "sw.js").replace(root, "…")}`);
57: }
58: 
59: // The Quarkus extension bundles the worker as a classpath fallback: its runtime
60: // classloader lives in the base runtime loader and may not see the consuming app's
61: // META-INF/resources copy. `ServiceWorkerFilter` prefers the app's copy, then this one.
62: const extensionResources = resolve(
63:   root,
64:   "../java/pathland-quarkus/src/main/resources/META-INF/resources/_pathland",
65: );
66: mkdirSync(extensionResources, { recursive: true });
67: const extensionWorker = resolve(extensionResources, "sw.js");
68: copyFileSync(resolve(root, "sw.js"), extensionWorker);
69: console.log(`copied -> ${extensionWorker.replace(root, "…")}`);

# pathland-spring-boot-starter — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 7, 2026

Spring Boot auto-configuration for Pathland: SSR at any path, live deltas over each
app's reserved `/{base}/ws`, per-session state. Adding the starter dependency + a
`PathlandApp` bean gives a running app; `MountedApp` beans host more apps at their own
subpaths (the BFF layout).

## Implemented

- **Security hardening (issue #63)**: the WebSocket handlers no longer hardcode
  `setAllowedOrigins("*")`. The default is Spring's same-origin handshake check
  (the WebSocket CSRF control); cross-origin hosts must be listed explicitly in
  `pathland.allowed-origins` (comma-separated). The handshake `wid` is validated
  by server-core (`WindowIds`). SSR inherits SRI (`integrity="sha384-…"`) from
  `PathlandSession`. CSP/security headers and transport limits are documented in
  `docs/HARDENING.md` (Quarkus supplies secure defaults; Spring apps add them
  through Spring Security/server configuration).
- **Hosted deployments work by default (issue #45 follow-up)**: a
  lowest-precedence `EnvironmentPostProcessor` contributes
  `server.forward-headers-strategy=framework`, so a TLS-terminating PaaS gets a
  correct WebSocket same-origin check and external SSR canonical URL with zero
  configuration. An explicit `server.forward-headers-strategy` in application
  config always wins (`ForwardedHeaderOverrideTest` pins this).
- **Topic hub bean**: `PathlandAutoConfiguration` produces a `PathlandSignalHub`
  bean (`host.signalHub()`: root mount, else the first mount) for external UI
  updates. `TopicSubscriptionsTest` mounts a `/topics` app and proves a
  background-thread publish reaches only the session subscribed for that subject.
- **Java host / Kotlin views**: `KotlinViewMountTest` proves a Java-only
  `@SpringBootApplication` bean returning `PathlandApp` mounts a Kotlin-authored
  fixture view, renders it through SSR, and receives a live signal delta.

- **Crawler endpoints**: `/robots.txt` (text/plain) and `/sitemap.xml` (application/xml) are real routes before the SPA catch-all, so Lighthouse does not parse the HTML shell as robots.txt.
- **SEO document head (issue #45)**: the SSR controller derives the canonical
  URL from the request and passes host-default `PageMetadata` to the registry;
  `PathlandApp.pageMetadata(...)` may override it per route before the first
  paint. Canonical/OG/Twitter/JSON-LD are on by default and configurable via
  `pathland.seo.{enabled,site-name,image,og-type,twitter-card,twitter-site,structured-data}`.

- **`PathlandAutoConfiguration`** (`@AutoConfiguration`, `@EnableWebSocket` since Spring
  Boot 3.5 no longer auto-enables it) + `META-INF/spring/…/AutoConfiguration.imports`:
  - default `StateStore` bean (`@ConditionalOnMissingBean` — Redis-or-in-memory),
  - `PathlandHost` bean (shut down with the context): every `MountedApp` bean plus the
    lone `PathlandApp` bean mounted at `/` (unless an explicit `MountedApp` claims the
    root). Without any app the host is empty and the starter is inert.
  - a `WebSocketConfigurer` registering **one handler per app** at its framework base
    (`/_pathland/ws` for the root, `/{mount}/_pathland/ws` otherwise). Each connection
    gets a fresh `uiId` (its UI model) + the client's `wid` (per-window state scope)
    from the WS `?wid=` query param (kept in `sessionStorage`, never in the page URL),
  - `PathlandIndexController` (SSR catch-all dispatching to the longest-mount app with
    the prefix stripped + a framework static controller serving the bundle + asset mount
    from `classpath:/static/_pathland/**` at both `/_pathland/**` and `/{app}/_pathland/**`;
    the more-specific mapping beats `/{*path}`, and the `!Upgrade` header excludes WS).
    When no static file matches, the controller serves renderer-owned assets from the
    shared Rust renderer: the content-hashed base stylesheet
    (`HtmlRenderer.baseCss()` at `baseCssName()`) as `text/css` with
    `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, and
    `/_pathland/icons/{name}.svg` glyphs (`HtmlRenderer.iconSvg` →
    `pathland_html_icon_svg`) with an `immutable` cache header — no static CSS/icon
    files on any host, and a host can still override either with a file. SSR links
    the CSS via `PathlandSession` → `renderLinked`.
    The framework controller honors byte-range requests (`206 Partial Content` +
    `Content-Range`, `416` for unsatisfiable ranges, `Accept-Ranges` on the full
    response) — a `<video>` (a `MediaController`'s playback) seeking beyond its
    buffer issues a `Range`
    request, and answering it with a full `200` would make browsers restart the media
    at byte 0.
    SSR renders defaults (no session cookie — per-window state arrives over the WS).
- **SSR debug comments**: the host reads the `pathland.debug-html` property
  (`@Value("${pathland.debug-html:false}")`) and forwards it to each registry, enabling
  per-node HTML comments in SSR output when set.
- **Per-window-id service worker (opt-in, issue #155)**: `pathland.service-worker`
  (default `false`) forwards to the host; the SSR emits `data-pathland-service-worker`
  and the controller serves `{base}/sw.js` with `Service-Worker-Allowed: /` +
  `Cache-Control: no-cache` (a stable, uncached script the browser byte-compares).
- **`SpringConnection`** — adapts `WebSocketSession` to `PathlandConnection`.
  `AutoCloseable`: a failed send surfaces as a close (the session's
  `closeConnection` closes the underlying session) so the DOM client reconnects +
  `META::RESYNC` instead of silently stalling on an open socket.
- **Heartbeat** — the socket replies to a client `META::PING` with a `META::PONG`
  **at the transport layer** (through its `SpringConnection`, no actor/session
  dependency; spec/OPCODE.md §Transport heartbeat).
- **Observability (issue #62)** — `spring-boot-starter-actuator` supplies the
  `MeterRegistry`; auto-config builds a `MicrometerTelemetry` over it (decorated with

  UP with `activeSessions`/`mounts` at `/actuator/health`. The `pathland.*` meters are
  exposed at `/actuator/prometheus` (add `micrometer-registry-prometheus`).

# pathland-quarkus — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 7, 2026

Quarkus extension for Pathland: SSR at any path, live deltas over each
app's reserved `/{base}/ws`, per-session state. Adding this extension + a
`PathlandApp` CDI bean gives a running app; `MountedApp` beans host more apps at
their own subpaths (the BFF layout). Author the root view with
`pathland-view-core`'s Kotlin DSL; Java hosts return Kotlin views from a
`PathlandApp` bean. The extension also provides the `dev.pathland.quarkus.kotlin`
capability and pulls in `quarkus-kotlin`.

## Implemented

- **Security defaults (issue #63)**: the deployment module contributes
  overridable runtime defaults via `RunTimeConfigurationDefaultBuildItem`:
  `quarkus.http.cors.enabled=true` (no origins → same-origin, which covers
  WebSocket upgrades because the CORS filter runs before routes),
  `quarkus.websockets-next.server.max-message-size`/`max-frame-size=65536`, and
  CSP + `X-Content-Type-Options`/`Referrer-Policy`/`X-Frame-Options` headers via
  `quarkus.http.header.*`. See `docs/HARDENING.md` for overrides, CSP rollout,
  reverse-proxy/TLS guidance, and edge rate limiting. The `wid` handshake query
  is validated by server-core (`WindowIds`). **HSTS is deliberately not an
  extension default** — it is a whole-origin, persistent browser policy that
  also covers other apps on the same server, so it is owned by the application
  or edge; the Quarkus demo opts in via `application.properties`.
  `docs/HARDENING.md` documents the directives and override guidance.
- **Hosted deployments work by default**: the same defaults set
  `quarkus.http.proxy.proxy-address-forwarding`, `allow-x-forwarded`, and
  `enable-forwarded-host` to `true`, so a TLS-terminating PaaS (Render, Fly,
  Heroku, Cloud Run) gets a correct same-origin WebSocket check and an external
  SSR canonical URL with zero configuration. These are lowest-priority defaults;
  application config (including
  `quarkus.http.proxy.proxy-address-forwarding=false`) always wins.
- **Topic hub bean**: the extension produces a `PathlandSignalHub` singleton
  (`host.signalHub()`: root mount, else the first mount) for external UI updates.
  `TopicSubscriptionsTest` mounts a `/topics` app and proves a background-thread
  publish reaches only the session subscribed for that subject.
- **Java host / Kotlin views**: `CounterApp` is a Java CDI bean whose
  `newRoot()` returns a Kotlin-authored fixture view; the multi-session
  WebSocket tests prove SSR + live deltas work through that mount.

- **Crawler endpoints**: `/robots.txt` (text/plain) and `/sitemap.xml` (application/xml) are real routes before the SPA catch-all, so Lighthouse does not parse the HTML shell as robots.txt.
- **SEO document head (issue #45)**: `IndexResource` derives the canonical URL
  from `UriInfo` and passes host-default `PageMetadata` to the registry;
  `PathlandApp.pageMetadata(...)` may override it per route before the first
  paint. Canonical/OG/Twitter/JSON-LD are on by default and configurable via
  `pathland.seo.{enabled,site-name,image,og-type,twitter-card,twitter-site,structured-data}`.

- **`PathlandSocket`** — `@WebSocket("/_pathland/ws")` for the root app: 1:1 sessions
  per connection (a fresh `uiId` per connection + the client's `wid` state scope from
  the `?wid=` query param), binary events routed into the root registry of the
  `PathlandHost`. **Stateless (critical)**: quarkus-websockets-next endpoints default
  to `@Singleton` — one shared instance for all connections — so the per-connection
  ids come from `connection.id()` + the handshake and the `QuarkusConnection` adapters
  live in a map keyed by connection id. Memoizing `uiId`/`wid`/`transport` on the
  shared instance collapsed every connection onto ONE session (multiple browsers shared
  one UI model — a probe or second tab drove the first tab's session).
- **`MountedPathlandSocket`** — `@WebSocket("/{app}/_pathland/ws")` for mounted apps:
  the `{app}` path param resolves the app's registry. Mount paths are single-segment.
  Same stateless rule as the root socket.
- **`IndexResource`** — JAX-RS SSR catch-all (`/` + deep links; `/_pathland/**` and the
  Quarkus non-application root `/q/**` — health/metrics — excluded via negative lookahead)
  dispatching to the longest-mount app (prefix stripped);
  SSR renders defaults (no session cookie — per-window state arrives over the WS);
  per-app framework files (`/{app}/_pathland/...`, e.g. the mounted app's bundle) are
  served from the shared `/_pathland/**` classpath mount. Quarkus serves the global
  `/_pathland/**` bundle + asset mount from `META-INF/resources` before JAX-RS.
  **`/_pathland/{name}.css`** (global JAX-RS route + the mounted-base
  `frameworkFile` path) serves the renderer-owned content-hashed base design
  (`HtmlRenderer.baseCss()` at `baseCssName()`) as `text/css` with
  `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`. **`/_pathland/icons/{name}.svg`**
  serves the renderer-owned icon glyphs from the shared Rust renderer
  (`HtmlRenderer.iconSvg` → `pathland_html_icon_svg`) with an `immutable` cache
  header — no static CSS/icon files on any host. SSR links the CSS via
  `PathlandSession` → `renderLinked`.
- **`PathlandRegistryProducer`** — CDI `@Produces @Singleton` `PathlandHost` from every
  `MountedApp` bean plus the lone `PathlandApp` bean (mounted at `/`); `@Disposes` shuts
  it down. Reads the `pathland.debug-html` config property (default `false`) to enable
  per-node HTML comments in SSR output, and `pathland.service-worker` (default `false`)
  to opt the DOM client into the per-window-id service worker (issue #155) — served at
  `{base}/sw.js` with `Service-Worker-Allowed: /` + `Cache-Control: no-cache`.
- **`ServiceWorkerFilter`** — serves `/_pathland/sw.js` (root and mounted bases) with
  `Service-Worker-Allowed: /` + `Cache-Control: no-cache`, so the client's root-scoped
  registration succeeds. A `Filters` handler always runs before routes, so it wins over
  Quarkus's static-resource handler (which sends neither header, and whose configured
  max-age would otherwise cache the script and delay update detection). The script is
  resolved through the thread-context classloader first, then the extension's own
  loader, then the system loader: extension runtime classes live in Quarkus's base
  runtime classloader and cannot see the application's `META-INF/resources` copy. The
  extension jar bundles the worker as a fallback (the TS copy script writes it), and
  `pathland-quarkus-demo`'s integration test asserts the headers on both the root and a
  mounted base — the packaged-app classloader path the module-local test could not see.
- **Observability (issue #62)** — `quarkus-micrometer` (a `MeterRegistry` bean) +
  `quarkus-smallrye-health`: the producer builds a `MicrometerTelemetry` over the
  registry and decorates it with `TracingTelemetry` when a `Tracer` bean is present and
  `quarkus.otel.enabled` (default `true`; the extension never touches the OTel API when
  the extension is absent/disabled). `PathlandHealthCheck` (`@Readiness`) reports the
  host UP with `activeSessions`/`mounts` at `/q/health`; the `pathland.*` meters appear
  at `/q/metrics`.
- **`QuarkusConnection`** — adapts `WebSocketConnection` to `PathlandConnection`.
  Sends are **serialized** (one `sendBinary` subscription in flight, the rest queued),
  and a **send failure closes the connection** so the session drops it and the DOM
  client reconnects + `META::RESYNC` (recoverable) instead of silently stalling on an
  "open" socket that never delivers (the remote seekbar symptom). **Send timeout**: a
  `sendBinary` that neither completes nor fails within 10 s (a half-dead connection /
  a dropped proxy upstream leg) is marked failed and closed — a hung send would
  otherwise wedge the serialized drain forever. **Keep-alive pings**: the connection
  sends a WS-protocol ping every 15 s (browsers auto-pong) to keep the connection warm
  through middleboxes and detect a dead client; `close()` stops the keep-alive
  scheduler (the sockets' `@OnClose` calls it).
- **Heartbeat** — both sockets reply to a client `META::PING` with a `META::PONG`
  **at the transport layer** (through their `QuarkusConnection`, no actor/session
  dependency, and a PING never creates or wakes a session); spec/OPCODE.md
  §Transport heartbeat.
- **Failure handling** — `fail()` logs the reason; `close()` (socket `@OnClose`)
  no longer calls `close()` on the already-closed connection (no spurious
  "Connection already closed" noise). A **transient write failure on a connection
  that still reports open is logged, not closed** — only a confirmed-dead channel
  (or a send hung past the timeout) warrants closing. The send-timeout task is
  **cancelled when the send completes**, so a completed-but-late callback can't
  false-time-out and kill a healthy connection. Keep-alive pings are sent directly
  (Vert.x serializes writes — no sync with `sendBinary` needed).
- `META-INF/beans.xml` so Quarkus discovers the extension.
- **Quarkus extension metadata** — runtime + `pathland-quarkus-deployment`; the
  runtime provides the `dev.pathland.quarkus` capability. The runtime has no
  dependency on the authoring DSL. Tests use Kotlin-authored fixture views to prove
  a Java CDI bean can mount them.

## App DX

public class MyApp {
    @Produces @Singleton PathlandApp main() { return () -> new MyHomeView(); }
    @Produces @Singleton MountedApp support() { return MountedApp.of("/support", ...); }
}
```

in the SSR model the client only ever receives the chosen destination's
  deltas.
- `Router` owns a `Signal<Route>` plus a **back-stack** and exposes
  `navigate` / `push` / `pop` / `replace` / `back`. `push` appends; `pop` /
  `back` step back; `navigate` / `replace` set the current route. The current
  path is emitted as the `ROUTE` property on the container slot.
- The route is a **plain signal — not persisted**. On the web the URL is the
  persistence layer (the DOM client mirrors it via `pushState`/`popstate`); on
  native the route is per-session.
- The initial route is delivered as a **`META::ENVIRONMENT` `ROUTE` field**
  (host → guest platform environment, OPCODE.md — the same message that carries
  the viewport): on SSR the host synthesizes it from the HTTP request (the
  request path — all the request offers), and over the WebSocket the DOM client
  sends it (with the viewport) as its **first** message; a reconnect re-sends it.
  The application applies the environment
  uniformly — the router hydrates from the `ROUTE` field before mount, so a
  deep-link request renders the right destination on the first frame. The app
  never models the platform's location handling — history adaptation
  (`pushState` / `replaceState` / back) is a renderer/DOM-client translation of
  the `ROUTE` property and the `NAVIGATE` event.

**Reserved framework root** — the host reserves **`/_pathland/**`** for its own
system endpoints, so app routes never collide with them: the WebSocket lives at
`/_pathland/ws`, the DOM-client bundle under a **content-hashed name**
(`/_pathland/dom-renderer-<sha256>.js`; the current name is published next to the
copies in the pointer `/_pathland/dom-renderer.current` (name + SRI digest), read by the SSR
layer so the page always references the built artifact — the fresh URL per build
busts immutable asset caches), the
renderer-owned icon glyphs at `/_pathland/icons/<name>.svg` (served from the
shared HTML-renderer library — `pathland_html_icon_svg` over the C ABI — which
the DOM client lazily fetches when a delta references an `ICON_NAME` the page
did not embed), and the host's asset mount at `/_pathland/assets/**`. App routes
are everything else (served by the SSR catch-all). The DOM client reads the
base from the SSR page's `data-pathland-base` attribute (default `/_pathland`),
so a host can relocate it behind a proxy. Asset references in the UI model are
**absolute** (`/_pathland/assets/icons/home.svg`) so deep-linked routes resolve
correctly.

**The `Navigation` facade** — the ergonomic entry point. `Navigation.navigator`
collapses the route table + router + seeding into one readable flow, and
`Navigation.container(router)` is the container:
=== TS README 45-75 ===
npm test          # vitest (happy-dom): codec round-trips, TREE/STYLE apply, transport
npm run build     # tsc --noEmit + esbuild -> dist/pathland-dom-renderer.js (IIFE, minified)
npm run copy-to-demos   # copy the bundle into the Java demos' static dirs
```

The per-window-id service worker has a real-browser E2E (Chromium + WebKit) — the
worker-engine differences (e.g. WebKit reporting an empty `clientId` on navigations)
are invisible to jsdom, so they are guarded here:

```bash
npx playwright install chromium webkit   # one-time

## The bundle

`dist/pathland-dom-renderer.js` is served by the Spring Boot and Quarkus (Java + Kotlin) demos under a
content-hashed name — `dom-renderer-<sha256>.js` (copied into each demo's static
resources by `npm run copy-to-demos`, which also prunes stale copies and writes the
`dom-renderer.current` pointer manifest the SSR layer reads to emit the `<script src>`).
The fresh URL per build busts the immutable asset cache.

## Transport resilience

`src/transport.ts` reconnects with exponential backoff, keeps the connection
alive with a `META::PING`/`PONG` heartbeat + no-activity watchdog, and recovers
from lost deltas: a **sequence gap** (a batch whose per-stream `sequence` breaks
the chain) makes the client skip the gapped batch and request a full snapshot
(`META::RESYNC`). See `spec/OPCODE.md` §Transport heartbeat and §Sequence gap
detection.

1: #!/usr/bin/env bash
2: # Sync the generated HTML base design into the Rust renderer crate.
3: #
4: # The canonical source lives in design/ (Style Dictionary tokens + hand-authored
5: # reset/components CSS). `design/build/base.css` is the generated bundle the
6: # renderer embeds with `include_str!`; `base.css.name` is its content-hashed
7: # asset name (served by the SSR starters). Run `npm --prefix design run build`
8: # first.
9: #
10: # Usage:
11: #   scripts/sync-design-css.sh           copy the bundle + name into the crate
12: #   scripts/sync-design-css.sh --check   fail if the committed crate copy drifted
13: set -euo pipefail
14: 
15: ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
16: SRC_DIR="$ROOT/design/build"
17: DEST_DIR="$ROOT/lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/assets"
18: FILES=(base.css base.css.name)
19: 
20: check=0
21: if [[ "${1:-}" == "--check" ]]; then
22:   check=1
23: elif [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; then
24:   echo "usage: $0 [--check]" >&2
25:   exit 2
26: fi
27: 
28: for file in "${FILES[@]}"; do
29:   if [[ ! -f "$SRC_DIR/$file" ]]; then
30:     echo "sync-design-css: missing $SRC_DIR/$file — run 'npm --prefix design run build' first" >&2
31:     exit 1
32:   fi
33: done
34: 
35: if [[ $check -eq 1 ]]; then
36:   for file in "${FILES[@]}"; do
37:     if [[ ! -f "$DEST_DIR/$file" ]]; then
38:       echo "sync-design-css: missing $DEST_DIR/$file — run scripts/sync-design-css.sh" >&2
39:       exit 1
40:     fi
41:     if ! diff -u "$DEST_DIR/$file" "$SRC_DIR/$file"; then
42:       echo "sync-design-css: crate $file is stale — run 'npm --prefix design run build && scripts/sync-design-css.sh'" >&2
43:       exit 1
44:     fi
45:   done
46:   echo "sync-design-css: up to date"
47:   exit 0
48: fi
49: 
50: mkdir -p "$DEST_DIR"
51: for file in "${FILES[@]}"; do
52:   cp "$SRC_DIR/$file" "$DEST_DIR/$file"
53:   echo "sync-design-css: wrote $DEST_DIR/$file"
54: done

(End of file - total 54 lines)
